newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile supermarket chain D&S to issue ADRs.
newsitem.headline: Chile supermarket chain D&S to issue ADRs.

text.p: Chilean supermarket chain D&S said it will increase its capital through the issue of 250 million shares which will be sold in local and international markets.

"It is the intention of the board that the placement of part of the new capital increase will be in foreign bolsas through the American Depositary Receipt (ADR) mechanism," said the company in a statement to the Stocks and Values Superintendency.
The company will hold a shareholders meeting July 14 to approve the increase, it said.
The new capital increase will annul most of a capital increase agreed by shareholders last year, said the statement.
D&S officials have said the firm will invest $500 million in the next four years in expanding its business in Chile and Argentina.
In Chile, the group owns the Almac, Ekono and Lider supermarket chains. The company has three stores in Buenos Aires and has a fourth under construction.
D&S will be the third Chilean supermarket chain to trade on Wall Street.
Valparaiso-based Santa Isabel issued ADRs in the mid 1990s, while Unimarc launched in New York this year.
